theme: Dispatch groups, work items and semaphores

terms.definition: A block of work packed in an object that you can run, wait for or cancel later.
terms.example: Cancel the dispatch work item before it starts.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let item = DispatchWorkItem { print("run") }
item.cancel()
item.perform()
print(item.isCancelled)

terms.definition: An object that tracks several tasks and tells you when all of them are done.
terms.example: Add every upload to one dispatch group.

terms.definition: A counter that lets only a fixed number of tasks use a resource at the same time.
terms.example: A dispatch semaphore limits the uploads to two.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let sem = DispatchSemaphore(value: 1)
sem.wait()
print("inside")
sem.signal()
print("free")

Learn to explain how to wait for many tasks and limit how many run: Dispatch Work Item, Dispatch Group & Dispatch Semaphore, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Dispatch Work Item - A block of work packed in an object that you can run, wait for or cancel later.
Dispatch Group - An object that tracks several tasks and tells you when all of them are done.
Dispatch Semaphore - A counter that lets only a fixed number of tasks use a resource at the same time.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Dispatch Work Item, Dispatch Group and Dispatch Semaphore in English?

dialogue.title: Three photo uploads
dialogue.setting: Uploading photos with a progress message

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I need to upload three photos and then show a message when all of them are done.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a dispatch group. A dispatch group tracks several tasks and tells you when they finish.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where do I put the upload code?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wrap it in a dispatch work item, like `item` in your code, and add it to the group.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why not use a plain closure?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A dispatch work item is an object, so you can cancel it before it starts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. And what if the server allows only two uploads at once?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then add a dispatch semaphore. It is a counter that limits how many tasks use the resource.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I thought `notify` waits for the semaphore too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, the dispatch group only counts its own tasks. The dispatch semaphore is a separate tool.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. The group tells me when we finish, and the semaphore limits the work.
Cancel the dispatch work item before it starts.
